# Rules of the Cairn diagram standard

Generated from `src/cairn/system/diagram/check.py` and `tokens.json`. The prose in
[`README.md`](README.md) is the standard; this file is the same rules as a checklist, and it is
generated so the two cannot disagree. A rule that exists in the checker and not here is a bug in
this file, and the generator refuses to write one.

Run `cairn diagram check <file>` to see which rules a description breaks. Nothing here needs a
model call or a network.

## Description rules

| Rule | What it requires | How to comply | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R1** | Title and scope | Start the title with the diagram kind from the token file; say in the scope what system or container the diagram describes, and for a computed view the commit and '0 model calls'. | checker: `cairn diagram check` |
| **R2** | One level per diagram | Every element belongs to the level in the title. A state among containers, or a component inside a container diagram, is a second diagram. | checker |
| **R3** | Element fields | Every element states a name, a type from the token file, a one-line responsibility, and its technology where the type requires one. Entities, code and states carry no responsibility. | checker |
| **R4** | Labels | Every arrow says what passes and why, never 'Uses' or 'Data'. 'How' (protocol, route or mechanism) is required at container, component and flow level and forbidden at context level. Keep 'what' and 'how' inside the token file's character budgets. | checker |
| **R5** | Line styles | sync, async, build and return are the four styles; reply is for flows only and build-time never appears inside one. | checker |
| **R6** | One direction per arrow | No two-headed arrows. Draw two labelled arrows, each with its own label, and never a second arrow duplicating the first in reverse. | checker |
| **R7** | Evidence and provenance | Every element and arrow cites at least one source: repo/path:line, a manifest or deploy entry, or the document or person that declares it. References are resolved against the working tree when the repository is present. Never name a credential. | checker (references resolved when `--root` is given) |
| **R8** | Budgets | Stay inside the node, relationship and boundary budgets in the token file, or split into an overview and a detail, or collapse a group into one box with a count and say so in the scope line. | checker, reading the budgets from tokens.json |
| **R9** | Boundaries | A boundary states what it isolates or owns, and is drawn only where such a fact exists. No layout bands, no overlap, no person or outside system inside the product boundary. | checker |
| **R10** | Legend | The legend stays on. Every diagram carries one, below it, listing only what that diagram uses. | checker |
| **R11** | Accents | At most the token file's number of accented elements. Accent marks focus, it does not decorate. | checker |
| **R12** | Known elements | Every arrow, participant, fragment and boundary refers to an element the diagram actually has. | checker |
| **R13** | Text alternative | One sentence saying what the diagram shows. It becomes the SVG's <desc> and the heading of the evidence table. | checker |

## Layout rules

No description can satisfy these and no YAML can express them, so they are not checker rules.
The renderer tests them on every render and the render command reports them:

- **No label overlaps another label or a box** — checked by the renderer's self-test, on every render.
- **No line passes behind a box** — checked by the renderer's self-test, on every render.
- **Rendered text is at least 7.5 px at the default size** — the token file's `font.min_rendered_px`.
- **Every colour role meets its contrast ratio against the paper** — checked by the renderer's self-test.
- **Labels sit on an opaque mask beside their line** — the `label_mask` role; enforced by the layout pass.

## Diagram kinds

The title prefix and the technology rule for each kind. 'Primary' is what the diagram is about;
'supporting' is what may sit outside it.

| Kind | Title starts with | Primary | Supporting | 'How' on arrows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `landscape` | System landscape | system, external-system, person | - | optional |
| `context` | System context | system | person, external-system | forbidden |
| `container` | Containers | container, data-store, channel, library | person, system, external-system | required |
| `component` | Components | component | container, data-store, channel, library, person, system, external-system | required |
| `flow` | Flow | - | - | required |
| `code` | Code | code | - | optional |
| `data-model` | Data model | entity | - | forbidden |
| `state` | Lifecycle | state | - | forbidden |

## Arrow styles

| Style | Dash | Head | Means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sync` | solid | filled | Synchronous request |
| `async` | async | open | Asynchronous message |
| `build` | build | open | Build-time dependency |
| `return` | return | filled | Reply (flows only) |

## Provenance marks

| Mark | Provenance | Means |
|---|---|---|
| (none) | `extracted` | Read directly from code, manifest or deploy file |
| ◆ | `declared` | Declared by a person (system.yaml or a hand-made source) |
| ≈ | `inferred` | Derived; verify before relying on it |
| ? | `ambiguous` | More than one candidate; see evidence |
| ⚠ | `stale` | Evidence no longer found at the last sync |

## Overlays

An overlay adds one fact without a new level, which is why it replaces a whole diagram.

| Overlay | Values | Colour role | Means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-class` | public, internal, personal, sensitive | `sensitive` | Data classification carried by the relationship |
| `trust-boundary` | - | `trust` | Boundary with a security control (authentication, network isolation) |

## What a Mermaid rendering cannot guarantee

See [`mermaid.md`](mermaid.md) for the whole picture. In short: Mermaid's own layout and theme
decide the picture. There is no legend inside a Mermaid diagram, labels crowd, an asynchronous
and a build-time arrow look alike on GitHub, there is no hover evidence, and a file has one
theme. Use Mermaid where native rendering matters; use `cairn diagram render` where the
standard must hold exactly.
